speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe your episodic cough and shortness of breath in detail, including when they started and what triggers them. To begin our assessment, have you noticed any fever, chest pain, or changes in your sputum?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old female. The patient reports a 1-month history of episodic cough and shortness of breath. The cough is nonproductive and worsens when climbing stairs and at night. She experienced fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion 8 weeks ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Asthma.

The patient's history of episodic cough and shortness of breath worsening at night and with exertion, following an upper respiratory infection, is classic for post-infectious reactive airway disease. Given the nonproductive nature of the cough and the specific triggers, do you have any history of childhood asthma or family history of allergies? I will also request a Chest_X-Ray to rule out other causes.
